excerpt: Find Selenium elements with plain English, using a 24 MB local model. No LLM, no API key, ~30 ms per lookup. - penielny/selenia
content_html:
Stop maintaining brittle XPath. Find Selenium elements with plain English, using a 24 MB model that runs locally. No LLM, no API key, no per-call cost.

A real run: every element is chosen by the model from the page's own elements.
🎯 89% top-1 / 96% top-3 on websites the model never saw during training
⚡ ~20–35 ms per find on a laptop CPU (Apple M1), after a one-time 0.4 s model load
🔒 100% local nothing leaves your machine; works offline and in locked-down CI
🛑 Never guesses raises when nothing fits, or when two elements fit equally well

Why Selenia?

Locators break whenever the front end changes: a renamed class, a moved div, a regenerated id. LLM browser agents can avoid that, but they need an API key, send your pages to a third party, cost money on every step, take seconds per action, and can confidently pick the wrong element.

Selenia does one job: it turns a description into an element. A small fine-tuned ranking model scores the real elements on the page against your description and returns the best one. It never writes a selector, so it cannot invent one.

Selenia LLM agents (browser-use, Stagehand, Skyvern…) Hand-written XPath / CSS
Survives UI refactors ✅ ✅ ❌
Runs offline, no API key ✅ ❌ (unless you host an LLM) ✅
Cost per step $0 API tokens $0
Latency per element tens of ms seconds ms
Same page + same description → same element ✅ ❌ ✅
Refuses ambiguous matches ✅ ❌ n/a
Plans multi-step tasks on its own ❌ ✅ ❌

If you want an autonomous agent, use an agent. If you want reliable, fast, free locators inside the Selenium tests you already have, use Selenia.

📦 Installation

pip install selenia

Or from source:

pip install .

🛠️ Usage

from selenium import webdriver
from selenia import Selenia

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
selenia = Selenia(driver)   # downloads the model on first use

driver.get("https://www.saucedemo.com/")
selenia.find("username field").send_keys("standard_user")
selenia.find("password field").send_keys("secret_sauce")
selenia.find("the login button").click()

# Find all matching elements, best match first
buttons = selenia.find_all("add to cart button")

find returns a normal Selenium WebElement, so it works alongside your existing code, waits and page objects. Elements inside open shadow DOM are found too.

More runnable scripts, including a full checkout flow, error handling and a pytest suite, are in examples/.

🎯 How matches are chosen

  • find raises Selenium's NoSuchElementException when the model is not confident (min_score, default 0.5) or when two elements fit equally well (min_margin, default 0.05). The message names the candidates, so you can see what to add to the description.
  • find_all returns every element scoring at least min_score, best first.
  • Tune both with LocalRanker(min_score=..., min_margin=...); min_margin=0 always takes the top pick.
  • iframes are not searched: switch into the frame first, then call find.

🧩 The model

A cross-encoder (based on ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) fine-tuned on about 28,800 description/element pairs collected from real websites, then exported to int8 ONNX. It runs on onnxruntime and tokenizers, so there is no PyTorch dependency.

Held-out evaluation (161 queries, sites unseen in training) top-1 top-3 MRR
Base model, before fine-tuning 82.6% 93.8% 0.890
Selenia, shipped int8 ONNX model 89.4% 96.3% 0.933

The first time you create a Selenia, it downloads the model (about 24 MB) into ~/.cache/selenia and verifies its checksum. After that it runs offline.

  • SELENIA_CACHE_DIR changes where the download is kept.
  • SELENIA_MODEL_URL fetches from your own mirror instead of the GitHub release.
  • To use a model you trained yourself, pass LocalRanker(model_dir="training/models/selenia-ce") or set SELENIA_MODEL_DIR. That is the folder written by training/train.py.

Train it on your own app

The full pipeline that produced the model (collecting pages, labelling, generating descriptions, fine-tuning, int8 export and evaluation) is in training/. Retraining on screens from your own product is the fastest way to push accuracy higher for your tests.

🧪 Running Tests

python -m pytest tests/

The tests in tests/test_browser.py drive a headless Chrome against a local page and are skipped when Chrome cannot start. The ones that use the real model are also skipped unless a trained model is at training/models/selenia-ce or SELENIA_MODEL_DIR.

🤝 Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Especially useful: pages where Selenia picks the wrong element (open an issue with the URL and your description), so they can be added to the training and evaluation data.

If Selenia saves you from fixing a broken locator, a ⭐ helps other people find it.
